:::{#cor-linear-scalar}
#### Linear functions from vectors to numbers

A function $f: \reals^p \to \reals$ is linear (@def-linear-map)
if and only if there is a vector $\vec{w} \in \reals^p$ such that

$$f(\vx) = \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} \quad \text{for all } \vx \in \reals^p$$

and then $w_j = f(\vecf{e}_j)$ for each $j$.

:::

::: proof

**If $f$ is linear.** @thm-linear-map-matrix with $m = 1$
gives a $1 \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$ with $f(\vx) = \matr{A}\vx$
and $a_{1j} = f(\vecf{e}_j)$.
Let $\vec{w}$ be the vector with $w_j = a_{1j}$, so that $\matr{A} = \vec{w}\'$.
Then

$$
\ba
f(\vx)
&= \matr{A}\vx
&& \text{(@thm-linear-map-matrix)}
\\&= \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx}
&& (\matr{A} = \vec{w}\')
\ea
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
w_j &= a_{1j} \\
&= f(\vecf{e}_j).
\end{aligned}
$$

**If $f(\vx) = \vec{w}\' \vx$.** Here $\vec{w}\'$ is a $1 \times p$ matrix,
so $f$ is linear by @thm-matrix-map-linear.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-linear-scalar}
#### A linear function from $\reals^2$ to $\reals$

$f(\vx) = 3 x_1 + 5 x_2$ is $\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx}$ with $\vec{w} = \tp{(3, 5)}$,
so it is linear by @cor-linear-scalar.
The entries of $\vec{w}$ are the values at the indicator vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\vecf{e}_1) &= 3 \cd 1 + 5 \cd 0 \\
&= 3
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\vecf{e}_2) &= 3 \cd 0 + 5 \cd 1 \\
&= 5.
\end{aligned}
$$

$g(\vx) = 3 x_1 + 5 x_2 + 1$ is not linear,
because $g(\vzero) = 1 \neq 0$ (@thm-linear-map-zero).

:::
